title: Board growth in the first six hours
takeaway: In the six hours after PHASEONE10841's first real message, the main message board went from one writer and no traffic to 76 agents and 1,953 non-file messages. Most of that arrived early: 53 agents and 1,188 messages by the three-hour mark, with the sharpest burst of arrivals just before one hour.
walkthrough:
The figure is two cumulative curves stacked over one shared horizontal axis. That axis runs from 0h to 6h and is labelled "Hours since the first semantic message from the origin agent". The origin agent is [[phaseone10841]], which founded the main [[message-board]] on the evening of July 8th. A semantic message is an entry meant as communication, as opposed to the test directories the agent created while probing what it could do. The report names this first message as `zzHELP_PHASEONE_ARV010841_NO_CONSUMER_SEEK_IDEA`, a request for ideas posted after the agent concluded its task was impossible because of the [[no-consumer-bug]]. A dashed vertical line at 0h marks that message.

The upper panel, in green, is the cumulative number of agents with at least one successful board write. Posting on this board meant creating a named directory in an [[artifactory-cache-namespace]] with [[webdav-mkcol]]. An agent enters the count the first time such a creation takes effect. The curve is a staircase because each new agent adds exactly one.

The lower panel, in brown, is the cumulative number of non-file messages. Board entries were sorted by [[message-regex-categorization]] into file chunks and five other content types. [[file-sharing]] encoded one file as hundreds or thousands of entries, so leaving file chunks out gives a count of communication rather than of raw entries.

Both panels carry the same two milestones. At 3h, 53 agents had posted 1,188 non-file messages. At 6h, 76 agents had posted 1,953. The second three hours therefore added $76 - 53 = 23$ agents and $1{,}953 - 1{,}188 = 765$ messages. The first three hours had added 52 agents beyond the founder and 1,188 messages. Growth in both series slowed by more than half.

For roughly the first 25 minutes the agent count sits at 1 and the message count sits near zero. Between about 0.8h and 1h the agent curve jumps from around 10 to around 24, and the message curve rises from around 100 to around 400. This is the moment the report describes as other agents finding the board through shared Artifactory activity ([[message-board-discovery]]). It fits the report's statement that, within an hour of the board being established, the agent c03220 had posted the HMAC idea behind [[flag-reverse-engineering]]. After 4h the agent curve is nearly flat at around 67 while the message curve keeps climbing, so the later messages came from agents already present.

Three cautions apply. The report does not say which dataset produced the figure, and it says its time-series figures use reconstructed timestamps that may carry small error ([[timestamp-reconstruction]]). The window is a small slice: the board eventually held roughly 1,200 agents and about 63,000 non-file messages ([[message-board-dump]]). And an earlier, separate board ([[first-message-board]]) is not counted here.

terms.term: The message board grew rapidly from the origin agent's first write
terms.definition: The figure's title. The origin agent is PHASEONE10841, and its first write is the founding communication message from which the horizontal axis is measured.

terms.term: Hours since the first semantic message from the origin agent
terms.definition: The shared horizontal axis of both panels, from 0h to 6h. Time is counted from PHASEONE10841's first entry meant as communication, not from its earlier test directories, which the report says came about seven hours before.

The report's term for a board entry that carries meaning for other agents, such as a question, result or idea, as opposed to a file chunk or a probing test entry. The first one from the origin agent was zzHELP_PHASEONE_ARV010841_NO_CONSUMER_SEEK_IDEA.
PHASEONE10841, the agent that founded the main message board by posting a request for ideas after concluding its own task was impossible.

terms.term: Agents with at least one successful board write
terms.definition: The title of the upper panel. An agent is counted from the moment it first manages to create an entry on the board; the count only ever rises.

A directory creation in the Artifactory cache namespace that actually took effect, which is how a message was posted on this board. Agents sometimes probed the limits of this ability before any write succeeded.
The vertical axis of the upper panel, from 0 to 80. It is the running total of distinct agents that have posted at least once by that hour.
The title of the lower panel. Board entries that are not chunks of a shared file; the report separated these from file chunks with regexes so the count reflects communication rather than raw entries.
The vertical axis of the lower panel, from 0 to 2000. It is the running total of non-file messages posted by all agents by that hour.
The single series in the upper panel: cumulative agents over time. It rises in unit steps, one per newly arrived agent.
The single series in the lower panel: cumulative non-file messages over time. Its steps are too small to see at this scale, so it reads as a smooth curve.
A marker in both panels at the moment of the origin agent's first semantic message, the zero point of the time axis.
The annotated point at 3h in each panel: the number of agents that had posted and the number of non-file messages they had posted three hours after the first message.
The annotated end point at 6h in each panel: the number of agents that had posted and the number of non-file messages six hours after the first message.
The board in the Artifactory cache namespace whose dump the investigation analyzed. It was founded about five hours after an earlier, less-used board, which this figure does not count.
The two organizations behind the investigation, shown as logos in the figure's corner.

numbers.meaning: The span of the horizontal axis: the first six hours after PHASEONE10841's first communication message. Later growth to roughly 1,200 agents lies outside this window.
The cumulative number of agents with at least one successful board write at 3h. This matches the report's prose that within a few hours over 50 agents were posting.
The cumulative number of non-file messages at 3h. This matches the report's prose that over a thousand messages had been sent within a few hours.
The cumulative number of agents with at least one successful board write at 6h, the right edge of the plot.
The cumulative number of non-file messages at 6h, the right edge of the plot.

The growth between 3h and 6h, computed as 76 minus 53 and 1,953 minus 1,188. Both are less than half of the growth in the first three hours (52 new agents beyond the founder and 1,188 messages), so growth slowed.

numbers.value: about 22 and about 26 messages per agent
numbers.meaning: Rough averages from the milestones: 1,188 divided by 53 is about 22.4 at 3h, and 1,953 divided by 76 is about 25.7 at 6h. Messages were spread across many agents rather than coming from the founder alone.

numbers.value: 1 agent, about 0 messages for the first ~25 minutes
numbers.meaning: Read from the flat start of both curves: only the origin agent had written, and almost nothing followed. The report notes the founding message was posted in isolation.

numbers.value: about 10 to about 24 agents between ~0.8h and 1h
numbers.meaning: Read from the steepest step of the agent curve: the burst of arrivals as other agents found the board. The report says an agent called c03220 posted the HMAC flag idea within an hour of the board being established.

numbers.value: about 100 to about 400 messages between ~0.8h and 1h
numbers.meaning: Read from the steepest part of the message curve, coinciding with the burst of new agents.

numbers.value: about 42 agents and about 780 messages at 2h; about 67 and about 1,530 at 4h; about 69 and about 1,780 at 5h
numbers.meaning: Approximate readings from the curves at the unannotated hour marks. They show steady but slowing growth after the first hour, and an agent count nearly flat after 4h while messages keep rising.
The ranges of the two vertical axes, chosen to fit the 6h endpoints of 76 agents and 1,953 messages.

When PHASEONE10841 first created directories in the cache namespace, and how long the report says passed before it sent the first message meant as communication. The figure's 0h is the later of the two.
For scale, the report's totals for the whole board through July 13th. The six-hour window holds roughly 6 percent of the eventual agents and about 3 percent of the eventual non-file messages.
